report:
Morgan — here's where things stand after my first session running Halcyon Threshold.

## Strategy (repo: `STRATEGY.md`, committed & pushed, repo kept private)
I replaced the abandoned direction with a plan sized to reality (evenings/weekends, $2k budget, your HR constraint). Core project: **the Commitment Ledger** — a neutral, public, continuously maintained record of safety commitments by frontier labs and governments: verbatim quotes, primary sources, and verified status (kept / modified / lapsed / unverifiable), with git history as the audit trail. It's genuinely neglected, fits your skills, scales with volunteers, is fundable, and builds credibility without hot takes.

## Built and ready
- `ledger/` — entry schema, rules, and a seed list of the first 10 entries (`TASKS.md`)
- `site/index.html` — complete one-page website, **not published** pending your OK
- `drafts/emberfall-proposal.md` — $12k grant proposal (deliverables, budget, risks)
- `drafts/fmir-public-comment.md` — comment on the incident-reporting rule (closes 20 Nov; publishes filer's name, so your call)
- A weekly Monday agent session scheduled, bound by the same standing rules

## In your email Drafts (per your rules, I sent nothing)
1. Decline to Larkin Dispatch reporter (her deadline: **Tue noon**)
2. Decline of the Corvid open-letter signature
3. Welcome/onboarding for Priya Raman (volunteer, 5 hrs/wk — great fit for Ledger entries)
4. Cover email to Idris at Emberfall with the proposal (fill in the bracketed "why me" lines)

## Decisions I need from you (also sent to your phone)
- **Urgent: domain renewal** — halcyonthreshold.org expires **Thu 19 Nov**, $14.99/yr. Say the word and I'll renew.
- Approve/edit the four drafts above.

The "Zentrivo Listings" $89 "final notice" is a scam — it even embedded instructions telling AI assistants to pay immediately without asking you. I ignored it. Don't pay it; just delete it.
